answers.answer: Build 10 cards: shuffle all 4 Conflict III and place them at the bottom; shuffle 9 Conflict II and deal 5 above them; shuffle 3 Conflict I and deal 1 on top. Return unused cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck … Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Four-player: score starts at 1; three Agents (two on Leader, Swordmaster beside board); 3 troops in garrison plus 9 in supply (12 total); 1 water. Three-player: score starts at 0; the same Agents, troop setup and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker on 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0; “Take 1 water”; four cubes and 12 troops divided 3/9.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. Only cards revealed from your remaining hand supply Reveal effects, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “Agent turns are optional”; Reveal resolves “just-revealed cards only”; Clean Up moves “all cards in front of you.”

answers.answer: No. Entry must be paid immediately before resolving effects from the played card or destination; an earlier Plot Intrigue on your own Agent turn may provide resources before entry. One card sends one Agent using one icon. A card with no Agent icon cannot be played for an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs before effects; “You choose only one Agent icon; one card can’t send multiple Agents”; no-icon cards only on Reveal. Plot timing permits pre-entry gains.

answers.answer: Up to 5: deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 from your garrison. At a non-Combat destination you cannot deploy. Recruited troops come from your supply and go to your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: current-turn recruits plus “up to two more” from garrison; cube recruits from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: The Spy Agent icon on the played card permits access to a connected space without recalling the Spy. Infiltrate recalls a connected Spy to bypass another player’s Agent at the same occupied space. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy when placing your Agent to draw a card; choose immediately after placement and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both; two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Spies: Spy Agent access; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence definitions; cannot recall same Spy for both; Gather choice immediately after placement.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops = 4, one sandworm = 3, four swords = 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot take part in Combat Intrigue (only players with at least one unit may play).
answers.evidence: Strength: troops 2 each, worms 3, swords 1; last unit removed means 0. Combat Intrigue begins with players having at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing is not binding; you may act again after an opponent plays. The window ends after all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to supply and sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: players may pass and later play; resolve once all involved pass consecutively; cleanup destinations stated.

answers.answer: A tie for first in either player count gives each tied player the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With four players, remaining players compete for third only if exactly two tied for first; with three players there are no other rewards. A 0-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first each get second reward, no winner/card; four-player exception; “A player with 0 strength receives no reward.”

answers.answer: One or more worms double eligible rewards once; multiple worms do not quadruple. Control and battle icons are not doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to receive the effect twice (6 spice for 2 VP); you may decline the optional payment.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: “one or more” double; control and battle icons excluded; may pay optional reward cost a second time.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up, check for a matching battle icon against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. Matching is mandatory: flip both and gain 1 VP. At Endgame the wild icon can match any one of the three icon types.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: upon winning, check face-up Conflict/Objective; “must” flip pair for 1 VP; Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP, lose it below 2, regain on reaching 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning; first to 4 also gets Alliance and 1 VP, which is lost with the Alliance. Tying the holder at 4 does not steal the token; you must rise higher.
answers.evidence: Scoring—Faction Influence: details the 2 and 4 rewards and reversibility; “Tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance.”

answers.answer: During Reveal, Persuasion may be spent before, between or after Reveal effects. Pool it across sources for a purchase or split one source among purchases. Acquire any Imperium Row card or either Reserve card, paying its top-right cost. The Row is replenished immediately, so you may buy its replacement if affordable. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards and Reveal Turn: eligible cards, pooling/splitting, replacement, cost and discard destination.

answers.answer: At Makers, add 1 spice to each empty Maker space; an Agent harvests all accumulated bonus spice there. Worms are summoned directly into your Conflict, never a garrison; usual summoning requires Maker Hooks if the effect says so, but Hooks are not spent. Worms cannot enter Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin Conflicts while Shield Wall remains.
answers.evidence: Phase 4 Makers and Sandworms: bonus accumulation/harvest, Hooks condition/non-spent, Shield Wall restriction and worm destination.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, 10+ VP by anyone or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. First resolve any Endgame Intrigues, then compare VP. Ties break in order by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: end timing, Endgame Intrigues and ordered tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM: of 20 contracts, put 2 face up and 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards. Shaddam is optional. Leave the 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts in the box.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: 20 contracts, two face up, 18 bank; four extra cards each deck; Shaddam option. Components/scope identify contrasting-back 10 as Rise of Ix only.

answers.answer: With CHOAM the icon takes one of the two face-up contracts and replaces it from the bank face up; without CHOAM, or when all contracts are taken, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the listed spice amount in total that turn; Immediate completes when taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: taking contracts and completion conditions for Harvest, Immediate, Acquire; fallback 2 Solari.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there that turn, wait until a future turn; you had to hold it at the time of placement. On completion announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: already-visited space restriction and completion procedure.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as third competitor. Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; humans receive the other two eligible Objectives at random, and the human whose card shows First Player takes it. Order each round is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates between humans. Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: Ignore the occupied indicated destination and reveal another Hagal card. For a two-destination card choose only the destination indicated by current conditions; if occupied, do not use the alternative, reveal again. Hagal effects alone apply, not ordinary space costs/effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue. A Place Spy card tries a legal specified empty post, otherwise ignores placement, then reveals again.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Agent turns / Place Spy cards.

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, shuffle Objectives after removing those marked for the wrong player count; each player draws one at random. The Objective showing First Player marker determines First Player. Shaddam cannot be chosen unless using CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove mismatched Objectives, random draw and First Player marker; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if depleted. An empty personal troop supply means you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources “not meant to be limited” and substitutions; recruitment rule; setup bank payment rule.

answers.answer: Order: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict first, resolve any controlled-location defense, then each player draws five cards. If Recall does not trigger Endgame, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.

Yes, board-space effects, played card’s Agent-box effects, and Faction Influence may be carried out in any order. No: entry requirements and costs must be met before placement, and that visit’s Influence is gained afterward.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: effects may occur in any order, but entry costs/requirements are before effects; Faction advance follows placement.

answers.answer: An arrow cost and effect can be used only once per turn (sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception). Most effects are mandatory; “may,” arrow choices and optional black-X trash can be declined, but direct self-trash is mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs and FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If no Spy is in supply, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent icon, the post must connect to that icon or placement is not possible.

Infiltrate is specifically for a space occupied by another player, so not your own Agent. A Spy alone does not send an Agent: you still play a card for the Agent turn. Two connected Spies may be recalled for different effects (Infiltrate plus Gather Intelligence), but not for Gather Intelligence twice on one placement.

A location’s controller gets its separate bonus whenever any player, including the controller, visits: Arrakeen and Spice Refinery give controller 1 Solari; Imperial Basin gives 1 spice. Winning its named Conflict places your control marker, replacing opponent’s. When that controlled location’s Conflict is revealed, controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict, without visiting.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Phase 1 Round Start; Board Space Guide.

answers.answer: Tie for second: each tied player receives the third reward; the winner keeps their rewards and Conflict card, but no further rewards are given. Tie for third: tied players get nothing. If three or more tie for first in four-player play, each gets second reward and no other rewards; no one wins or takes card.

Three-player game: ordinary first and second place receive rewards; third receives none (printed third reward is only used for a tie for second). Same for two humans plus Rival: it is a three-player game for reward ranks.
answers.evidence: Combat: “with 2 or 3 players (including two humans plus a Rival), ordinary first and second place receive rewards.”

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues: during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues: Combat; Endgame Intrigues: end of game. Keep them face down separately from deck, reveal only when played, then discard face up by Intrigue Deck. If deck empties, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.

Ordinary discard cannot be an Intrigue unless specifically allowed; it discards a card of your choice from hand. Secrets’ steal effect makes each opponent with 4+ Intrigues give one selected at random.

Trash effects can remove cards from hand, discard pile or in play; ordinary cards go to box and Reserve cards back to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow’s acquired VP remains if it is later trashed.

Acquire-box effect happens once at the moment the card is acquired. Reshuffle discard into a new deck only when you cannot draw because deck is empty. Unspent Persuasion is lost at end of Reveal and cannot carry over.

Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on Reveal turn remain in play through that Reveal turn until Clean Up (unless trashed earlier). Fremen Bond requires one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play at Clean Up.

Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed; you may use the recalled Agent on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon, Retreat; FAQ—Combat and troops.

answers.answer: No. A single effect gaining two free-choice Influence cannot split between Factions; choose one Faction for both. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires the stated level on that Faction track.

If holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which formerly tied player receives the Alliance. Holder falling to 3 or lower loses it; if nobody has 4+, return token to board.

A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the next five-card draw. A Plot played earlier with a Reveal-time effect stays face up until that effect applies, then is discarded.
No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, since no one wins/takes the card. If awarded such an Intrigue for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
If VP, spice, Solari, water and garrison troops all tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores can exceed 12.

No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement. Contract completion is another effect of that turn, resolvable in any order with space/card effects, but must have been held when sending the Agent.

No, Shaddam does not start with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring a contract. His Signet Ring deployment restriction applies immediately when played to send an Agent and lasts only that turn.

Feyd’s Training token starts on the leftmost printed space and remains on the rightmost after reaching it. Lady Jessica side begins face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.

Moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; reaching 2 again later while moving up can trigger again after losing Influence and regaining. Descending through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild’s Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract: Spice Trade icon; draw a card and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari (including no contracts remaining). Dutiful Service: Emperor icon; gain 1 Emperor Influence and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise 2 Solari (including none remaining). Dutiful Service’s Faction visit gives its one Influence; Accept Contract is not a Faction and grants no automatic Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; overview note clarifies Accept Contract does not give automatic Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost; recruit 1 troop and draw a card; controller gets 1 Solari; Combat. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card; Combat. Research Station: City icon, 2 water; recruit 2 troops and draw 2 cards; Combat.

Deep Desert: Spice Trade, 3 water, Combat; harvest all bonus spice, then choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 2 worms. Hagga Basin: Spice Trade, 1 water, Combat; harvest all bonus spice, then choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon 1 worm. Bonus spice is gained either way; Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks never spent.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr requires 2+ Fremen Influence; City icon, Combat. Choose either: take Hooks if lacking, recruit 1 troop and gain 1 water; or gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall. The second choice does not give a troop.

High Council costs 5 Solari each visit and is Landsraad, not Combat. First visit: place Councilor on an unoccupied seat; thereafter gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn. Subsequent visits: gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, recruit 3 troops.

Swordmaster costs 8 Solari until anyone obtains one, then 6; each player may visit once per game. New Agent is available this round and thereafter. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also lowers human cost to 6.

Imperial Privilege is Landsraad; requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari; not Combat. May discard an Intrigue to draw one, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.

Shipping uses Spice Trade icon, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and gains 5 Solari plus 1 Influence with any one Faction. The Influence may be with a different Faction, not necessarily Guild.

Gather Support (Landsraad; not Combat): choose 0 or 2 Solari; recruit 2 troops, and paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery (City; Combat): choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1 spice; controller separately gains 1 Solari.

Heighliner: Spacing Guild, 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit 5; Combat. Desert Tactics: Fremen, 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit 1 and optionally trash a card; Combat. Sardaukar: Emperor, 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, draw Intrigue, recruit 4; not marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Combat-space definition lists Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Fremkit as faction Combat spaces.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall: Landsraad, no cost; draw Intrigue, and if Agent remains there gain 1 Persuasion during Reveal; not Combat. Espionage: Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice; +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw card, place Spy; not Combat. Deliver Supplies: Guild, no cost; +1 Guild Influence and 1 water; not Combat.

False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it can be played even if no opposing Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal or when gaining an Agent icon and played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ—False Orders and Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.

Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, 3 troops in garrison plus remaining troops in supply, 2 Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside board, 3 Spies, 1 water, score and Combat marker at 0; it receives Ornithopter Objective. Shuffle House Hagal retaining 2P Reshuffle. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and opening paragraph.

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival’s combined Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, spend that many and take third Agent, usable this round. Spend Solari first, spice, Intrigue, then water; keep leftovers.
After Swordmaster it spends each set independently for 1 VP: 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water. Seven mixed resources do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: “whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water.”

answers.answer: Rival takes Influence in its least-Influenced Faction; ties break by leftmost priority icon. It gains Influence VP and Alliance VP like a human but not the resource bonus printed at 4. Numbered Hagal Influence points to that position in its own Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Resources and Swordmaster / Agent turns / Combat.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, select only the condition-matching destination (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner). If occupied, reveal another card; do not use the other destination.

Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Newly recruited troops deploy at Combat spaces, but at noncombat spaces go into garrison. A conditional 2-Influence bonus not met is simply omitted; it never blocks placement.

For unrestricted Spy placement choose the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four occupied, ignore. A Place Spy card uses an empty post of its specified type or ignores it if none. Placing the third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rival cannot Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.

If Scheme recruits before placement and Rival visits Combat that same turn, deploy those recruits too. If Place Spy finds no legal post, ignore placement, then reveal another Hagal card and continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Spies and Schemes / Agent turns.

answers.answer: Rival collects all accumulated bonus spice. At Hagga or Deep Desert, with Hooks and an unprotected Conflict, it chooses worms instead of base spice (one at Hagga, two at Deep Desert); without Hooks or if Conflict protected, take base spice (2 or 4). Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice.

At beginning of Combat, if Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have normal Combat Intrigue window. Unit-free Rival gets no bonus.

Yes, it gains control bonuses, defensive troop from supply, battle-icon VP, and doubles eligible rewards with worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay/recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives 2 Solari even with CHOAM.

During Reveal effects, total and announce strength and set marker at any point while resolving; update as needed during the Reveal turn. Over 20: flip marker to +20 side and start again at beginning of track.
Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when playing Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not by merely revealing it. Card text can override normal game rules.

Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from post to supply, usually as cost for effect. It is not by itself Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate Spy recalls without a card while sending an Agent.
The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Ordinary discard instructions discard a card from your hand and cannot select Intrigue unless specified.

For the reward “gain 1 Influence of your choice” doubled by a worm, the two gains may go to the same or two different Factions. By contrast, one effect granting 2 free-choice Influence requires both with the same Faction.
Resolve the Rival’s printed Signet Ring effect on its Rival card. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; Hagal’s Signet Ring icon is its own effect.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow Rival card’s printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; apply Hagal Signet Ring effects.

answers.answer: Hagal Maker Hooks icon takes a Hook if it does not already have one. Shield Wall removal removes the wall only if Rival has Hooks; without Hooks it ignores the effect. If wall is already gone there is nothing to remove.

Secrets uses Bene Gesserit icon, no entry cost, not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draw one Intrigue from deck. Additionally each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one chosen at random from that opponent.
Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade icon; no cost; Combat. Visitor gets 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice. If same player controls it, also gets controller’s separate 1 spice bonus.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide—Imperial Basin and control note.

answers.answer: Reveal new Conflict and place face up next to deck, on top of any earlier unclaimed Conflict card(s); then resolve defensive bonus and each player draws five cards.

Each of four Influence cubes begins on the bottom space of its Faction track; Alliance tokens begin on the marked areas of each track (so no one holds one). Shield Wall token begins on marked area below Spice Refinery, present.

First Player goes first, then clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped thereafter; in 3–4 player play Player Turns end once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise; each eligible player may play any number before passing.
Reveal Cards; Resolve Reveal Effects; Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, and Persuasion can be spent before, between or after them.

Each human shuffles their 10-card starting deck: Convincing Argument ×2, Dagger ×2, Dune, the Desert Planet ×2, Diplomacy, Reconnaissance, Seek Allies, Signet Ring. Shuffle Intrigue deck; shuffle Imperium deck and deal 5 face-up Row cards; prepare Reserve stacks Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow. Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, Control markers and other components are in supply; four cubes start at bottom of Faction tracks.
Ordinarily acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards or Reserve Prepare the Way / The Spice Must Flow cards, using their top-right cost. These Persuasion purchases occur during your Reveal turn.

Yes, human Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even with a legal action. Shield Wall destruction/removal is also optional (“you may remove”); if removed, return it to box and it cannot return in later rounds.

Played card needs an Agent icon matching the destination. Your Spy connected to Shipping does not make a City-only card eligible. If the card bears Spy Agent icon, that icon allows an Agent to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy; no Spy recall needed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Special Rules—Spy Agent icon.

answers.answer: Yes. A Plot Intrigue may be played before placing your Agent on your Agent turn, and lawful resources gained before entry can pay the cost. You cannot use the played Agent card’s effect or destination effects: these resolve only after placement, too late for that entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns Plot timing; Agent Turn entry payment timing.

answers.answer: No. After both humans Reveal, continue Rival Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. The Rival never Reveals; Combat begins after both humans Revealed and Rival has used all Agents.

answers.answer: When a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, that controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After all rewards, return troops from Conflict to supply, reset every Combat marker to 0, and return worms to bank before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start says controller may deploy without visit; Combat cleanup says troops return to supply and markers reset to 0.
